In Support of:
LD 17, An Act to Designate the Warden of the Maine State Prison as Chief Administrative Officer of the Bolduc
Correctional Facility

Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Criminal
Justice and Public Safety, I am Tony Cantillo, Deputy Commissioner of the Maine Department of Corrections (DOC) providing testimony today in strong support of LD 17, An Act to Designate the Warden of the Maine State Prison as
Chief Administrative Ofiicer of the Bolduc Correctional Facility. As further explained below, this bill is a simple house keeping proposal to help us better manage Department resources. The Department thanks Senator Beebe-Center for sponsoring this bill on our behalf.

The proposal before you today represents an effort by our Department to optimize the management of resources between Maine State Prison (MSP) and Bolduc Correctional Facility (BCF). As discussed during our orientation presentation last
week, BCF is one of three pre-release facilities operated by our Department. BCF houses residents at minimum or community custody levels who have five years or less left on their sentence. Residents of BCF may participate in
connnunity-based work release, education, and other community-based programs. MSP, on the other hand, is the State's sole maximum-security facility, which houses residents at custody levels of medium or greater.
Those who have spent time visiting MSP or BCF will be familiar with how closely the two facilities are located. The
facilities are a less than three minute drive apart and the properties are connected by a contiguous land mass. This
closeness in proximity means that MSP and BCF are ofien looked at as if they are one unified campus. They share staff and programming resources, and residents from MSP ofiten transition to BCF when they reach the appropriate custody level. However, MSP and BCF are established separately and with separate leadership in Maine statute. BCF is established under Title 34-A, Chapter 3, Subchapter 9 and MSP is established under Title 34-A, Chapter 3, Subchapter 2,
both with distinct leadership structures.

For two facilities that operate in such close proximity with overlapping resources, this separation creates some awkwardness is managing those resources. The separation results in the facilities being managed under separate budgets and it also slows down the process of staff from one facility stepping in to provide support for the other facility when needed. Speaking of the budget, you' ll also notice that this proposal aligns with our 26-27 Biennial Budget proposal to unify the finances for these facilities. This separation results in more paperwork and less administrative flexibility when compared to a campus like Maine Correctional Center, where the secure facility at the top of the hill and the Southem
Maine Women's Reentry Center at the bottom of the hill are managed as a single campus.

The bottom line is that we are seeking this change in order to allow the Department to be more efficient with our
management of resources. The director of BCF will continue to oversee BCF and the warden of MSP will continue to
oversee MSP. This change will simply allow for the more efficient sharing of staff, financial resources, and material resources in a similar way to how we currently manage campuses at Maine Correctional Center and Mountain View
Correctional Facility.

For the reasons stated above, the Department respectfully asks for the committee's support in this proposal.
This concludes my testimony. I am happy to answer any questions.

Anthony Cantillo Deputy Commissioner Maine Department of Corrections

Good Afternoon Representative Hasenfus and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Criminal Justice and Public Safety. As you know, I am Senator Beebe-Center, and I am here
today to present a bill that I have agreed to partner on with the Maine Department of Corrections,
LD 17, An Act to Designate the Warden of the Maine State Prison as Chief Administrative
Officer of the Bolduc Correctional Facility.
This bill is a simple, common sense, proposal to help the department better manage its resources.
Currently, Maine State Prison and Bolduc Correctional facility are established under separate
sections in Maine Law that require the facilities to have separate leadership and separate
management of financial resources, material resources, and staff.
This separation might surprise you if, like me, you've ever spent time visiting these facilities. Maine State Prison and Bolduc Correctional Facility are located right next to each other. This closeness results in the facilities sharing many resources and operating in close coordination. It would be easy assume that the facilities operate like a single campus in the same way as Maine
Correctional Center and Southern Maine Women's Reentry Center. However, that is not the case.
As the department will address in more depth following my testimony, this separation creates
some unnecessary complications for the operation of these facilities. It makes sharing of financial resources more cumbersome and it impedes the efficiency of staff stepping in to help out when needed. The bill before you today solves those problems by formally Lmifying the facilities in statute as one unified campus. According to the department, this bill will not result in any other meaningful change to the operation of these facilities.
This concludes my testimony. While I'd be glad to answer any questions the committee has, it
may be better to wait and ask those questions of the Department, who will be up next to explain
this bill in more detail.
Thank you

The Warden of the Maine State Prison, as the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), holds significant responsibility for overseeing the operations of the prison. This role includes ensuring the safety and security of both inmates and staff, enforcing institutional policies, managing daily activities, and adhering to legal and regulatory requirements. The Warden's position is pivotal in maintaining order, providing rehabilitation programs, and ensuring compliance with ethical and legal standards in the correctional system.
The Warden, as the CAO, must exhibit strong leadership and management skills, addressing challenges such as inmate behavior, staffing shortages, resource allocation, and public safety. Additionally, the Warden must be accountable for responding to incidents within the facility, from conflicts among inmates to potential security breaches.
In an opinion about the Warden's role, one might emphasize the importance of balancing the enforcement of strict rules with efforts to rehabilitate inmates. There's also the matter of transparency and communication with the public, particularly when dealing with allegations of abuse or neglect. The Warden is expected to create an environment that upholds human dignity while ensuring that the objectives of the correctional system -- punishment, deterrence, rehabilitation, and public safety -- are met.
